subject: Commit term and credit-split proposal — LumenAI (Reserved Capacity)
messages:
From: Alicia Reyes <alicia@lumenai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenai.com
Date: 2026-09-22T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — LumenAI (draft)

Marissa / Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — LumenAI's infra and product teams are aligned on moving forward with a reserved capacity pilot. Attached is a draft SOW and an initial sensitivity workbook (lumen_sensitivity.xlsx) that shows three GPU-price scenarios and how our consumption shapes across the pilot.

High level ask: we want an 18-month committed pool that covers our projected 200k token-hour usage/month at burstable headroom. Given the current GPU market noise, procurement is asking for two pricing safety options:

- Option A: 12% up-front credit against committed spend, paired with a 10% overage rate when usage exceeds the pool.
- Option B: Smaller up-front credit (6%) and a monthly credit schedule (applied as bill credits tied to on-time payments).

Procurement is nervous about downside (GPU prices drop) and upside (GPU prices spike). They asked whether Redwood can offer an indexation clause or a credit-split that adjusts if GPU costs move beyond +/- 20% vs the benchmark.

Attached: LumenAI_SOW_v1.pdf; lumen_sensitivity.xlsx

Can you confirm what approval path / discount bands we should expect on your side, and whether Redwood can accept a short form clause tying unit pricing to a public GPU index? We need to present options to Lumen's CFO by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Alicia Reyes
Head of Infrastructure, LumenAI
Alicia | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — LumenAI (draft)

Alicia — thanks for the materials and the clear ask. Looping in Sean and our finance lead David so we can get a recommendation quickly. A couple of immediate notes from a sales/ops perspective:

- We can do an 18-month commit; our go-to is to offer either an up-front credit or a monthly amortized credit, but the exact % and whether it's refundable/escrowed depends on deal size and discount band.
- For indexation: we can support a GPU-index clause, but it requires a defined benchmark and a trigger band (e.g., +/- 15% or 20%) and a pre-agreed remediation (credit, price reduction, or contract re-opener). Legal will want precise language.
- Approval path: discounts up to 12% can be approved by Sales Ops; anything >12% requires Finance + Sales leadership sign-off; >20% needs Exec approval. David — can you confirm those bands and whether we can propose a hybrid credit-split (part upfront / part monthly) that is contingent on a GPU-index trigger?

Alicia — we'll come back with two structured proposals tomorrow (one conservative, one more customer-favorable) and the required approver list so you can take it to your CFO.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alicia / Marissa — quick working idea from Sales:

We propose two concrete options for your CFO to evaluate:

1) Balanced Split (recommended)
   - 18 month commit; 30% credit applied up-front as a non-refundable prepayment credit; remainder amortized monthly over the term.
   - If GPU-index moves up >20% compared to the benchmark, Redwood guarantees access to an additional 10% burst buffer at the same unit price for the next 3 months (to avoid immediate throttling).
   - If GPU-index moves down >20%, we automatically apply a downward price adjustment of up to 8% to the committed unit price and issue a pro-rated credit for future invoices.

2) Conservative (procurement-friendly)
   - 18 month commit; 12% up-front credit + monthly 2% credits tied to on-time payment.
   - Indexation clause limited to upward adjustments only (i.e., in a GPU spike Redwood absorbs half of the delta up to +15%; beyond that we trigger an escalation review).

Approval/esc. path (for internal use):
- Discounts <=12%: Sales Ops approval (Kimberly).
- Discounts 12–20% or structural add-ons (burst buffer guarantees): Finance + Head of Sales sign-off (David + Marissa).
- Discounts >20% or legal indexation with refund language: Exec review (CRO/CEO).

Action items:
- David, can you run the profitability delta for option 1 vs option 2 using the attached sensitivity workbook? (Lumen supplied three GPU curves; we need NPV impact).
- Kimberly, please prepare an approver checklist and the Slack escalation path for exceptions.

Alicia — if that looks reasonable I'll formalize language and circulate a short-term clause for review (one paragraph indexation + trigger thresholds + remediation).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team / Alicia — I ran the scenarios in the attached pricing_matrix.csv and the key takeaways: 

- Option 1 (Balanced Split) has higher short-term cash plus modest downside protection. Under the worst-case GPU prices (GPU spot down 30%), the NPV impact to Redwood is roughly -2.2% vs baseline — manageable. Under a +30% GPU spike, absorption of the first +20% would cost ~3.8% margin in Q1 but the burst buffer access reduces churn risk.
- Option 2 (Conservative) preserves our margins better in upside scenarios but reduces early cash flow in the first two quarters.

Approvals: current guardrails are accurate — finance will approve structural discounts up to 12% and contractual credits up to the proposed levels. Any deal that requires an effective discount >20% or refundable escrow requires Exec review (CRO + CFO). Also: indexation clauses that allow downward price adjustments will need legal to sign off and a precise public benchmark. Suggestion: use 'Public GPU Index (PGI) - average weekly spot across major clouds' and set symmetric trigger at +/-20% with remediation options (credit vs price re-opener).

Draft contract language (summary):
"If the PGI moves more than 20% up or down relative to the baseline week prior to contract execution, either party may request a price adjustment discussion. For downward movements beyond 20%, Redwood will apply a downward adjustment up to 8% to committed unit pricing and credit the customer's account on a pro-rated basis; for upward movements beyond 20%, Redwood will provide a temporary burst buffer at the agreed committed price for up to 3 months while parties negotiate an equitable adjustment."

I'll attach the pricing matrix and can produce an exec-ready 1-pager showing NPV and cash-flow for both options. Kimberly — please add required approvers and timelines to the checklist. Alicia — happy to join a 20-minute CFO call to walk the math if helpful.

Thanks,
David Kim
